slides.title: Background on Mayor Joe Anderson's School Payments
bullets: Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, claimed £4,500 per year from Chesterfield High School, Merseyside, despite doing nothing for pupils.
A Labour mayor who campaigned against austerity while being paid an £80,000 salary took £4,500 per year from a school where he previously worked, despite doing nothing for pupils.
The payments were made despite Mr Anderson's lack of involvement in the school's activities.
slides.speaker_notes: Mayor Joe Anderson's payments to Chesterfield High School have been a subject of controversy. He claimed £4,500 per year, despite doing nothing for the pupils. This is despite being paid an £80,000 salary.

slides.title: Attempt to Justify Payments
bullets: Joe Anderson attempted to justify the payments by saying he provided the school with 'kudos' for being linked to him.
However, the school stopped the payments in 2011, and Mr Anderson attempted to sue them, claiming discrimination because of his 'philosophical belief' in public service.
slides.speaker_notes: When the school stopped the payments, Mr Anderson claimed he was being discriminated against. However, the school argued that the payments were a misapplication of public monies.

slides.title: Judicial Ruling
bullets: In the most recent case, Judge Daniel Serota ruled that outsiders would consider the payments a 'misapplication of public monies' and that the school was right to stop them.
The judge stated that Mr Anderson's lawyers could not provide any clear benefits the school received in return for the payments.
slides.speaker_notes: The most recent case was heard by Judge Daniel Serota, who ruled in favor of the school. The judge stated that the payments were a misapplication of public monies and that the school was right to stop them.

slides.title: Conclusion
bullets: The payments were made despite Mr Anderson's lack of involvement in the school's activities.
The school stopped the payments in 2011, and Mr Anderson attempted to sue them, claiming discrimination.
The most recent case ruled in favor of the school, stating that the payments were a misapplication of public monies.

A Labour mayor who campaigned against austerity while being paid an £80,000 salary took  £4,500 per year from a school where he previously worked, despite doing nothing for pupils.

evidence.chunk_content:
Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, claimed £4,500 per year from Chesterfield High School, Merseyside, despite doing nothing for pupils .

A Labour mayor who campaigned against austerity while being paid an £80,000 salary took  £4,500 per year from a school where he previously worked, despite doing nothing for pupils.

Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, attempted to justify the payments by saying he provided the school with 'kudos' for being linked to him.

Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, attempted to justify the payments by saying he provided the school with 'kudos' for being linked to him.

And when Chesterfield High School in Crosby, Merseyside, stopped the payments in 2011, he attempted to sue them, claiming discrimination because of his 'philosophical belief' in public service.

The details of the case, published in The Times, came after Mr Anderson rejected an employment tribunal ruling against him and took his case to appeal, which was also rejected.

In the most recent case, Judge Daniel Serota ruled that outsiders would consider the payments a 'misapplication of public monies ' and that the school was right to stop them.

He added that he had repeatedly asked Mr Anderson's lawyers to state what benefits the school got in return for their cash.

He said: 'The only answer that I received was that it gave 'kudos' to the school.' Mr Anderson had been a senior learning mentor at the school from 2001, when he was already a Liverpool councillor.
